pathway.title: Primo Brands Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Primo Brands earned slightly less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Net sales for nine months 2026 were USD 5,243.3 million, up 2.6%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,102.0 million, down 1.0%, and the margin was 21.0% against 21.8%. Cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight, materials and depreciation, and the filings flag tariffs and supply chain disruption as continuing cost risks. Q3 2026 was better: net sales rose 3.1% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to USD 411.0 million [Financial base, Business context].

Leverage is moderate on the company's definition and materially higher without add-backs. Total debt before unamortized costs was USD 5,249.7 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash was USD 477.2 million, giving net debt of USD 4,772.5 million. On trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million that is 3.66x gross and 3.32x net. On trailing EBITDA of USD 1,209.1 million before USD 227.0 million of add-backs it is 4.34x gross and 3.95x net. Add-backs are shrinking as integration costs wind down, from USD 365.1 million in FY2025 to USD 124.4 million in nine months 2026, but they are still management-defined. Net leverage was 3.37x at year-end 2025 and 3.32x at 2026-09-30, so the improvement is small and came mainly from a USD 100.5 million rise in cash [Financial base].

Cash flow improved, but part of the gain is working capital. Operating cash flow was USD 625.3 million for nine months 2026 against USD 477.2 million, of which USD 141.1 million came from payables and accruals, which can reverse. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million against USD 203.4 million. Cash interest paid was USD 200.4 million, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest of USD 298.7 million 4.81x [Financial base].

Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging. Dividends of USD 131.2 million and buybacks of USD 70.1 million took USD 201.3 million, 63% of nine-month free cash flow. Over the trailing twelve months dividends and buybacks of USD 364.1 million were about equal to free cash flow of USD 362.1 million. The board approved a new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million on 2026-11-03 and declared a dividend of USD 0.12 a share. The sponsor affiliate sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026 and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about USD 10.0 million. The stockholders agreement gives the sponsor approval rights over large dividends, most repurchases and debt that would take total net leverage above 3.5x while it holds at least 30% of the shares; its holding after August 2026 is not disclosed, so whether those rights still apply is unknown [Financial base, Business context].

Liquidity is ample and the maturity wall sits later than the term loan. Liquidity of USD 1,063.8 million is USD 477.2 million of cash plus USD 586.6 million of revolver availability after USD 163.4 million of letters of credit, with the revolver assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of undrawn availability. The term loan was refinanced to March 2031 at a SOFR margin of 2.75%, up from 2.25%. The derived ladder puts USD 532.3 million due in 2028 and USD 1,490.2 million in 2029, mainly the 3.875%, 4.375% and 6.250% notes, against USD 2,943.2 million in 2031. The revolver matures in February 2030 with a springing maturity whose condition is not stated, and the company says it does not expect operating cash flow to repay all debt at maturity [Financial base].

Security and covenants favour the secured lenders and are only partly tested. About 82.3% of debt before unamortized costs, the term loan and the two secured note series, ranks first lien, and 13.6% is the unsecured 6.250% notes (Calculations). The revolver's first lien net leverage covenant of 5.00x and interest coverage covenant of 2.00x are printed, the company states compliance, and neither reported ratio nor definition is supplied. A management-basis proxy puts first lien net leverage at 2.68x and interest coverage on the expense basis at 4.50x, which shows direction only [Financial base, Source readiness].

Business concentration and claims are unsized. One customer was about 21% of FY2025 net sales, regional spring water was 50.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales, and the same category is the subject of the Patane labelling class action. A securities class action and a consumer delivery class action are also pending, and the company estimates no loss beyond amounts accrued. Operating leases of USD 612.1 million are outside the debt figure [Business context, Financial base].

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and brands: a vertically integrated North American network of more than 50 production facilities and more than 200 depots, with regional spring water, purified water and premium water brands, and growth in premium water of 31.7% for nine months 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Liquidity: USD 1,063.8 million at 2026-09-30, no facility expiring within twelve months, and a term loan refinanced to March 2031 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cash generation: free cash flow of USD 319.6 million for nine months 2026, up from USD 203.4 million, and trailing cash interest cover of 4.81x on Adjusted EBITDA [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Falling add-backs: USD 124.4 million for nine months 2026 against USD 262.5 million, as integration winds down [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Creditor protections: first lien security for the term loan and secured notes, a sponsor veto on leverage-increasing debt while the holding is at least 30%, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release in 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management states the objective of reducing net leverage [Management Language; Business context].

Weaknesses. Leverage depends on add-backs: 4.34x gross and 3.95x net before add-backs of USD 227.0 million against 3.66x and 3.32x after [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Margin pressure: gross margin of 29.9% against 31.1% for nine months 2026 on freight and materials costs [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Shareholder returns: USD 201.3 million of nine-month dividends and buybacks and a new USD 300.0 million program, alongside a small improvement in net leverage [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Maturity cluster: derived USD 2,022.5 million due in 2028 and 2029, and a springing maturity on the revolver with no stated condition [Analyst Interpretation; Financial base]. Concentration: one customer at about 21% of FY2025 net sales, with no 2026 update [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Asset quality: goodwill and intangible assets of USD 6,497.3 million are 60.0% of total assets and exceed stockholders' equity of USD 3,048.7 million, so tangible equity is negative [Analyst Interpretation; Calculations]. Unquantified claims: three class actions with no estimate beyond amounts accrued [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Documentation gaps: no credit agreement, indentures or stockholders agreement, so legal capacity to distribute or add debt cannot be tested [Insufficient Information; Source readiness].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no pending acquisition, disposal or merger in the sources, and no new bond issue in 2026. The one financing transaction in the period is the Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026, which refinanced term loans then outstanding at 3,067.6 into new term loans of 3,090.0 maturing in March 2031, repricing the SOFR margin to 2.75% from 2.25%, while the revolving credit facility of 750.0 is described as maturing in February 2030 subject to a springing maturity whose condition is not stated (Q3 10-Q page:16, page:17; 10-K page:156). The company recorded a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026. The three note series, the 3.875% Senior Secured Notes due October 31, 2028, the 4.375% Senior Secured Notes due April 30, 2029 and the 6.250% Senior Notes due April 1, 2029, date from exchange offers completed with new indentures on February 12, 2025, in which the issuers co-issued new notes for the original Primo Water Holdings and Triton Water Holdings series; holders who did not tender kept original notes whose covenants were largely removed (10-K page:158 to page:160). Ownership transactions are the other group. The November 8, 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water was accounted for as an acquisition of Primo Water with BlueTriton as accounting acquirer (10-K page:146). The sponsor affiliate sold shares in secondary offerings in March 2025 and May 2025 totalling 99,250,000 shares and again on August 7, 2026, when it sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share and the company, using cash on hand, bought 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 while receiving no offering proceeds (10-K page:46; Q3 10-Q page:19). The status of each is closed. After quarter end, on November 3, 2026, the board declared a dividend of 0.12 a share and approved a new repurchase program of up to 300.0 that replaces a program with 40.8 left (Q3 10-Q page:39); this is announced and unexecuted. The company also sold production facilities held for sale for gross proceeds of 41.3 in nine months 2026 and had agreements after December 31, 2025 to sell further facilities for combined proceeds of 38.3 (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:191). The nature of the nine-month acquisitions of 48.0 shown in investing cash flow is not described in the sources and stays Insufficient Information. The effect of any of these on leverage is limited: the refinancing raised principal by 22.4, the repurchases consume cash that would otherwise reduce net debt, and the facility sale proceeds are modest against total debt. How the company would fund a larger repurchase while keeping leverage near the level in the financial base is not stated.

fields.value: Primo Brands Corporation reports as one registrant with one segment, so the base is a single consolidated set of statements rather than a segment mosaic. Through nine months 2026, net sales were 5,243.3, up 2.6% on 5,109.9, and Adjusted EBITDA was 1,102.0, down 1.0% from 1,112.7, because cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight and materials costs (Q3 10-Q `page:49`). Q3 2026 was better than the first half: net sales rose 3.1% to 1,821.0, Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to 411.0 and the margin was 22.6% against 22.9% a year earlier. EBITDA before add-backs rose much faster than Adjusted EBITDA (396.9 against 313.1 in Q3) because lower integration costs (add-back of 23.7 against 88.2) and an unrealized gain of 26.1, both excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, flowed through, and the total add-backs shrank to 14.1 in Q3 2026 from 91.4 a year earlier. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,436.1 gives gross leverage of 3.66 times and net leverage of 3.32 times on the company's definition; on EBITDA before add-backs of 1,209.1 the ratios are 4.34 and 3.95 times. Cash paid for interest of 298.7 over the trailing twelve months is covered 4.81 times by Adjusted EBITDA. Operating cash flow was 625.3 for nine months against 477.2, with payables and accruals contributing 141.1 of the 148.1 improvement, partly offset by other working capital lines; a payables-driven gain can reverse. Liquidity of 1,063.8 is cash of 477.2 plus revolver commitments of 750.0 less 163.4 of letters of credit. The March 2026 refinancing moved the term loan to March 2031, so the nearest large maturities are the 3.875% notes in October 2028 and the 4.375% and 6.250% notes in April 2029. Four limits bind: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure with large add-backs, covenant ratios are not printed, finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance are not itemized at September 30, 2026, and the maturity ladder after the refinancing is derived, not filed.

The ratings printed in the Q3 10-Q (`page:53`) are Corporate / Family "B1" and "BB-", Senior Secured "Ba3" and "BB", Senior Unsecured "B3" and "B", with "Outlook Positive Neutral"; they are company-reported statements, not independent rating documents.

fields.value: Net debt fell to 4,772.5 at September 30, 2026 from 4,872.4 at December 31, 2025, a decrease of 99.9, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1,436.1 from 1,446.8. Net leverage on the company's definition was therefore 3.32 times against 3.37 times, a small improvement that comes from cash rising by 100.5 rather than from earnings growth; gross debt before unamortized costs was nearly unchanged at 5,249.7 against 5,249.1. Leverage was higher at the March and June 2026 test dates (3.52 and 3.42 times net) because unrestricted cash (287.9 and 366.5) and trailing Adjusted EBITDA (1,411.3 and 1,429.6) were both lower then. On unadjusted EBITDA, which includes integration costs and unrealized gains, trailing leverage is 4.34 times gross and 3.95 times net, so the difference between the two bases, 0.68 times gross and 0.63 times net, measures how much of the credit story rests on add-backs. The add-backs fell from 365.1 in FY2025 to 124.4 in nine months 2026, which supports management's view that integration costs are winding down (Q3 10-Q `page:49`), but the "other adjustments, net" line is still 11.5 in nine months 2026 against (5.0) in nine months 2025 (Q3 release `page:11`).

Interest and financing expense, net for nine months 2026 was 239.5, 3.1% lower than 247.1 a year earlier (Q3 10-Q `page:50`), even though the term loan margin rose to 2.75% from 2.25% at the refinancing (Q3 10-Q `page:16`; 10-K `page:156`); the swaps fix the rate on 500.0 of the term loans and one of them ends December 31, 2026. Cash interest paid of 200.4 was below the expense of 239.5 for nine months; non-cash amortization of debt discount and issuance costs of 21.5 (Q3 10-Q `page:6`) explains part, and the timing of semi-annual coupons in April and October (10-K `page:159`, `page:160`) is a consistent but unstated explanation for the rest, which is an inference. These ratios are not the covenant measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow from continuing operations was 625.3 for nine months 2026, up 148.1. The company attributes this to improved earnings excluding non-cash charges of 80.1 and an increase in cash provided by trade payables and accruals of 141.1, partly offset by larger uses for prepaid assets, receivables and inventories (Q3 10-Q `page:58`). A payables-driven gain can reverse. Receivables absorbed 163.5 in nine months 2026 against 133.4, and cash paid for income taxes rose to 112.0 from 56.8. Free cash flow was 319.6 against 203.4. Dividends of 131.2 and buybacks of 70.1 took 201.3 of it, leaving 118.3, about 37% of free cash flow, while cash rose by 100.5. The adjusted free cash flow of 602.9 adds back 146.3 of acquisition, integration and restructuring cash costs and 101.8 of integration capital expenditure among other items (Q3 release `page:12`), so the gap between free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow of 283.3 is itself management-defined. Purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangibles were 305.7 for nine months 2026, 5.8% of net sales; the outlook's "Base CAPEX" of 4% of net sales is a separate management measure, so the two are not directly comparable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of 477.2 plus revolver availability of 586.6 gives 1,063.8, against current portion of long-term debt of 74.4 and nine-month cash interest of 200.4. The revolver matures February 2030, so no facility expires within twelve months, but the springing maturity condition is not stated and could shorten it. The company states that it does not expect to generate sufficient cash from operations to repay at maturity the entirety of its debt and so depends on refinancing (Q3 10-Q `page:51`). The revolver is assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of "undrawn availability" and no revolver borrowing line appears in the financing cash flows; that is an inference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA is defined by management as net income from continuing operations before interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization, adjusted for acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses, stock-based compensation, unrealized gains and losses on foreign exchange and commodity forwards, loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment, debt modification losses, purchase accounting and other adjustments (Q3 10-Q `page:43`). Four points matter. First, the integration add-back of 91.2 for nine months 2026 is larger than the statement line of 47.5 because 43.7 of integration cost sits in cost of sales (Q3 release `page:11`, `page:12`). Second, Q3 2026 operating income of 248.9 includes other operating income of 28.0, of which 27.6 is unrealized gains on commodity forwards (Q3 10-Q `page:47`); Adjusted EBITDA removes 26.1 of unrealized gains, against unrealized gains of 27.6 in Q3 2026 and 1.8 in Q3 2025 in operating income, so part of the rise in operating income is a mark-to-market swing. Third, depreciation and amortization fell to 146.3 from 163.1 in Q3 2026, mainly because amortization of customer lists and definite-lived trade names fell to 30.1 from 56.1 (Q3 release `page:12`), which lifts net income without any cash effect. Fourth, FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA excluded insurance proceeds of 47.3 and added back an intangible asset impairment of 35.6 (10-K `page:86`). The effective tax rate was 28.4% for nine months 2026 against 36.4% (Q3 10-Q `page:50`).

That wording is too strong. The notes lines of the fair-value table are carried net of unamortized discounts (the 10-K states discounts of 7.5 on the 3.875% notes and 31.7 on the 4.375% notes at December 31, 2025, `page:155`), while the term loan line is principal. The 232.2 therefore mixes finance leases, other debt not in the table and note discounts. It is still not decomposed in the Q3 10-Q, and the gap about finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance stands, but the 232.2 should not be read as unitemized debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands operates one segment: a vertically integrated North American branded water business with retail distribution to more than 200,000 outlets and a recurring direct-to-consumer arm made up of Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill. Revenue is split about evenly between regional spring water and everything else, premium water is the fastest-growing category, and one retail customer accounted for about a fifth of FY2025 net sales, which is the main concentration disclosed. Margin is exposed to freight, materials and tariff costs, and integration costs are fading but still sit in cost of sales. There is no pending sale, merger or acquisition in the sources. The transactions that matter to a creditor are historical or financial: the November 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water, the March 2026 term loan refinancing, a series of sponsor secondary offerings with company repurchases alongside them, and a new repurchase program approved on November 3, 2026. The sponsor affiliate held about 32.0% of voting power in February 2026 and the stockholders agreement gives it approval rights over large dividends, share repurchases and added debt above a stated leverage level while it holds at least 30% of the Class A shares; its present holding after the August 2026 sale is not disclosed, so those rights may or may not apply. Documented actions show cash returns to shareholders and a pre-combination dividend to the sponsor, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in 2026, although the February 2025 exchange offers stripped covenants and guarantees from original notes that were not tendered. Behaviour is therefore read as mixed on the evidence available, not as extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility cannot be separated without the credit agreement, the indentures and the stockholders agreement, none of which is in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no pending acquisition, disposal or merger in the sources, and no new bond issue in 2026. The one financing transaction in the period is the Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026, which refinanced term loans then outstanding at 3,067.6 into new term loans of 3,090.0 maturing in March 2031, repricing the SOFR margin to 2.75% from 2.25%, while the revolving credit facility of 750.0 is described as maturing in February 2030 subject to a springing maturity whose condition is not stated (Q3 10-Q `page:16`, `page:17`; 10-K `page:156`). The company recorded a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026. The three note series, the 3.875% Senior Secured Notes due October 31, 2028, the 4.375% Senior Secured Notes due April 30, 2029 and the 6.250% Senior Notes due April 1, 2029, date from exchange offers completed with new indentures on February 12, 2025, in which the issuers co-issued new notes for the original Primo Water Holdings and Triton Water Holdings series; holders who did not tender kept original notes whose covenants were largely removed (10-K `page:158` to `page:160`). Ownership transactions are the other group. The November 8, 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water was accounted for as an acquisition of Primo Water with BlueTriton as accounting acquirer (10-K `page:146`). The sponsor affiliate sold shares in secondary offerings in March 2025 and May 2025 totalling 99,250,000 shares and again on August 7, 2026, when it sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share and the company, using cash on hand, bought 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 while receiving no offering proceeds (10-K `page:46`; Q3 10-Q `page:19`). The status of each is closed. After quarter end, on November 3, 2026, the board declared a dividend of 0.12 a share and approved a new repurchase program of up to 300.0 that replaces a program with 40.8 left (Q3 10-Q `page:39`); this is announced and unexecuted. The company also sold production facilities held for sale for gross proceeds of 41.3 in nine months 2026 and had agreements after December 31, 2025 to sell further facilities for combined proceeds of 38.3 (Q3 10-Q `page:15`; 10-K `page:191`). The nature of the nine-month acquisitions of 48.0 shown in investing cash flow is not described in the sources and stays Insufficient Information. The effect of any of these on leverage is limited: the refinancing raised principal by 22.4, the repurchases consume cash that would otherwise reduce net debt, and the facility sale proceeds are modest against total debt. How the company would fund a larger repurchase while keeping leverage near the level in the financial base is not stated.

It gives the fundamental credit view from the source readiness, financial base and business context handoffs, using the Q3 2026 10-Q only to test figures in Calculations. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands Corporation's fundamental credit view is moderately cautious: a scaled branded-water business with improving cash flow and ample liquidity, but leverage that rests heavily on management add-backs and a cluster of note maturities in 2028 and 2029. The strongest support is USD 1,063.8 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, USD 625.3 million of operating cash flow in nine months 2026 and a term loan now due in March 2031. The weakest point is that trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million is slightly below year-end, leaving leverage at 3.66x gross and 3.32x net, or 4.34x gross before add-backs, while shareholder returns continue. Three things decide the outcome: how freight and materials costs are passed through, whether shareholder returns are balanced against deleveraging, and the refinancing of the 2028 and 2029 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primo Brands earned slightly less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Net sales for nine months 2026 were USD 5,243.3 million, up 2.6%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,102.0 million, down 1.0%, and the margin was 21.0% against 21.8%. Cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight, materials and depreciation, and the filings flag tariffs and supply chain disruption as continuing cost risks. Q3 2026 was better: net sales rose 3.1% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to USD 411.0 million [Financial base, Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate on the company's definition and materially higher without add-backs. Total debt before unamortized costs was USD 5,249.7 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash was USD 477.2 million, giving net debt of USD 4,772.5 million. On trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million that is 3.66x gross and 3.32x net. On trailing EBITDA of USD 1,209.1 million before USD 227.0 million of add-backs it is 4.34x gross and 3.95x net. Add-backs are shrinking as integration costs wind down, from USD 365.1 million in FY2025 to USD 124.4 million in nine months 2026, but they are still management-defined. Net leverage was 3.37x at year-end 2025 and 3.32x at 2026-09-30, so the improvement is small and came mainly from a USD 100.5 million rise in cash [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow improved, but part of the gain is working capital. Operating cash flow was USD 625.3 million for nine months 2026 against USD 477.2 million, of which USD 141.1 million came from payables and accruals, which can reverse. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million against USD 203.4 million. Cash interest paid was USD 200.4 million, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest of USD 298.7 million 4.81x [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging. Dividends of USD 131.2 million and buybacks of USD 70.1 million took USD 201.3 million, 63% of nine-month free cash flow. Over the trailing twelve months dividends and buybacks of USD 364.1 million were about equal to free cash flow of USD 362.1 million. The board approved a new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million on 2026-11-03 and declared a dividend of USD 0.12 a share. The sponsor affiliate sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026 and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about USD 10.0 million. The stockholders agreement gives the sponsor approval rights over large dividends, most repurchases and debt that would take total net leverage above 3.5x while it holds at least 30% of the shares; its holding after August 2026 is not disclosed, so whether those rights still apply is unknown [Financial base, Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample and the maturity wall sits later than the term loan. Liquidity of USD 1,063.8 million is USD 477.2 million of cash plus USD 586.6 million of revolver availability after USD 163.4 million of letters of credit, with the revolver assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of undrawn availability. The term loan was refinanced to March 2031 at a SOFR margin of 2.75%, up from 2.25%. The derived ladder puts USD 532.3 million due in 2028 and USD 1,490.2 million in 2029, mainly the 3.875%, 4.375% and 6.250% notes, against USD 2,943.2 million in 2031. The revolver matures in February 2030 with a springing maturity whose condition is not stated, and the company says it does not expect operating cash flow to repay all debt at maturity [Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Security and covenants favour the secured lenders and are only partly tested. About 82.3% of debt before unamortized costs, the term loan and the two secured note series, ranks first lien, and 13.6% is the unsecured 6.250% notes (Calculations). The revolver's first lien net leverage covenant of 5.00x and interest coverage covenant of 2.00x are printed, the company states compliance, and neither reported ratio nor definition is supplied. A management-basis proxy puts first lien net leverage at 2.68x and interest coverage on the expense basis at 4.50x, which shows direction only [Financial base, Source readiness].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business concentration and claims are unsized. One customer was about 21% of FY2025 net sales, regional spring water was 50.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales, and the same category is the subject of the Patane labelling class action. A securities class action and a consumer delivery class action are also pending, and the company estimates no loss beyond amounts accrued. Operating leases of USD 612.1 million are outside the debt figure [Business context, Financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and brands: a vertically integrated North American network of more than 50 production facilities and more than 200 depots, with regional spring water, purified water and premium water brands, and growth in premium water of 31.7% for nine months 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Liquidity: USD 1,063.8 million at 2026-09-30, no facility expiring within twelve months, and a term loan refinanced to March 2031 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cash generation: free cash flow of USD 319.6 million for nine months 2026, up from USD 203.4 million, and trailing cash interest cover of 4.81x on Adjusted EBITDA [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Falling add-backs: USD 124.4 million for nine months 2026 against USD 262.5 million, as integration winds down [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Creditor protections: first lien security for the term loan and secured notes, a sponsor veto on leverage-increasing debt while the holding is at least 30%, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release in 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management states the objective of reducing net leverage [Management Language; Business context].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage depends on add-backs: 4.34x gross and 3.95x net before add-backs of USD 227.0 million against 3.66x and 3.32x after [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Margin pressure: gross margin of 29.9% against 31.1% for nine months 2026 on freight and materials costs [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Shareholder returns: USD 201.3 million of nine-month dividends and buybacks and a new USD 300.0 million program, alongside a small improvement in net leverage [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Maturity cluster: derived USD 2,022.5 million due in 2028 and 2029, and a springing maturity on the revolver with no stated condition [Analyst Interpretation; Financial base]. Concentration: one customer at about 21% of FY2025 net sales, with no 2026 update [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Asset quality: goodwill and intangible assets of USD 6,497.3 million are 60.0% of total assets and exceed stockholders' equity of USD 3,048.7 million, so tangible equity is negative [Analyst Interpretation; Calculations]. Unquantified claims: three class actions with no estimate beyond amounts accrued [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Documentation gaps: no credit agreement, indentures or stockholders agreement, so legal capacity to distribute or add debt cannot be tested [Insufficient Information; Source readiness].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The source readiness handoff recorded no executed financing, lease or ownership documents, a pre-refinancing debt table and ladder, and unreviewed text extraction. The financial base added that the revolver balance, finance leases and other debt are not itemized at 2026-09-30, that the current maturity ladder is derived and that covenant ratios are not printed. The business context handoff judged this synthesis Ready with limitations and logged the sponsor-holding and stockholders-agreement gaps, so confidence stays below High. They are restated once in Gaps and not repeated as findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The credit view of the synthesis, moderately cautious with Medium confidence, follows from the cited basis and does not go beyond it. Four claims are only partly supported, each as wording or inference rather than figures: the remark that first-quarter earnings are structurally lower, the description of the largest customer as a retail customer, the description of the receivables build as seasonal, and the assumption that the revolver is undrawn, which the filing implies but does not print. No claim is unsupported and no contradiction between modules was found. The earlier readiness handoff described a residual of 232.2 as debt the Q3 report does not itemize; the financial base corrected that, and the correction is right. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is nonetheless Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most to a creditor, namely covenant headroom, the springing maturity, guarantor perimeter, sponsor consent rights over distributions and added debt, and the current maturity ladder, rest on documents and a filed schedule that are not in the sources. The review itself is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and the page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a moderately cautious view is that liquidity is 1,063.8, free cash flow is 319.6 against 203.4, add-backs have fallen to 124.4 from 262.5, net leverage has fallen from 3.52x in March to 3.32x, the company-reported ratings carry a positive outlook at one agency by column order, and management left Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance of 790 to 810 unchanged. If integration costs keep falling and freight costs ease, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could rise while shareholder returns stay within free cash flow. What would make that case win: fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of at least 363.0, the amount implied by the low end of guidance, adjusted free cash flow in the implied range of 187.1 to 207.1, repurchases staying below free cash flow, and early refinancing of the 2028 notes.

fields.value: Downside chain with observable triggers. Initiating condition: a freight, materials or tariff cost shock that pricing does not offset. First operational break: gross margin falling below the 29.9% of nine months 2026. Financial transmission: lower Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow while the dividend of 0.12 a share per quarter and the repurchase program continue. Leverage consequence: with net debt unchanged at 4,772.5, a fall of about 5% in trailing Adjusted EBITDA takes net leverage to 3.5x (Calculations), the level the stockholders agreement summary uses as a test. Liquidity and refinancing consequence: revolver drawings above the assumed nil balance would reduce liquidity below 1,063.8, and lenders would face the 3.875% notes due October 31, 2028 and the April 2029 notes with weaker cover. Triggers to watch: quarterly gross margin, add-backs, the revolver balance, repurchase pace against free cash flow, the sponsor's disclosed holding, and the covenant certificate when obtainable.
